nodes.name: Pt SA Deposition with Cl Ligands
nodes.procedure: Pt single atoms anchored on surface of RuOx-covered Ru nanoparticles (Ru-NPs@RuOx) using Pt precursor with Cl ligands via spontaneous deposition method (detailed synthetic procedure provided in Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: We have synthesized the Pt SAs anchored on the surface of RuOx-covered Ru NPs (Ru-NPs@RuOx) with and without the addition of Cl ligands (denoted as Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOx... detailed nomenclature in the Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Cl-free Pt SA Deposition on Ru Support
nodes.procedure: Pt single atoms anchored on Ru nanoparticles with partially oxidized surface (Ru-NPs@RuOx) using Cl-free Pt precursor via spontaneous deposition method.
nodes.source_text: For a comparison, we also synthesized the Pt SAs on Ru NPs@RuOx (Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOx) using Cl-free precursor.

nodes.description: Acidic HER LSV performance in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The acidic HER performance of Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ was evaluated in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ ... Figure 2a, the Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ catalyst without any reduction exhibits an initial HER overpotential (η) of 92 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², such an overpotential decreases during the HER process and finally approaches a stable value of 13.2 mV ... The Tafel slope (Figure 2b) for Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ is approximately 56.8 mV dec⁻¹ ... calculated exchange current density (j₀) ... ca. 5.7 mA cm⁻² ... mass activity (MA) at an overpotential of 50 mV ... 15.3 A mgPt⁻¹ ... turnover frequency ... at -0.05 V ... 15.1 H₂ s⁻¹

nodes.description: PEMWE MEA stability test at 1.0 A/cm²
nodes.source_text: MEA with Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ ... delivering a cell voltage of ∼1.66 V at 1.0 A cm⁻² and ∼1.76 V at 2 A cm⁻² ... MEA with Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ exhibits outstanding stability (Figure 2d), with a decay rate of only 17.8 μV h⁻¹ at 1.0 A cm⁻² over 1000 h

A durability comparison ... indicates that Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ exhibits the smallest MA loss after 24 h electrolysis ... During the early stage of the HER (0.5∼3 h) Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ catalyst experiences only a 7.2% decay in MA

nodes.source_text: in situ normalized Pt L₃ edge XANES spectra ... reveal the valence states of Pt decrease from 2.5 to -0.3 over 2000 s HER at a constant potential of -0.05 V versus RHE ... the Pt-Ru coordination signal emerges and gradually intensifies, accompanied by a significant increase in the CN_Pt-Ru (from 2 to 5). nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show uniform dispersion of Ru-NPs with average diameter of ca. 2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images (Figures S1 and S2) show the uniform dispersion of Ru-NPs with an average diameter of ca. 2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings demonstrate homogeneous dispersion of Pt and Cl elements on the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mappings (Figure S1b) further demonstrate the homogeneous dispersion of Pt and Cl elements on the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM confirms presence of isolated Pt single atoms on Ru-NPs with FFT showing Ru crystal facets (100), (101), and (002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inset fast Fourier transform (FFT, inset in Figure 1a) analysis derived from aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) image (Figures 1a and S3) of Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ exhibits three crystal facets of metallic Ru, corresponding to (100), (101), and (002), respectively.

properties.features: bright spot with diffraction-like pattern, labeled 101 100 002

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns verify metallic Ru NP bulk structure with crystal facets (100), (101), and (002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: which is also verified by X-ray diffraction patterns (Figure S4), confirming that the bulk structure is the metallic Ru NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Cl 2p identifies two Cl species: Pt-Cl ligand (ClPt 2p3/2 at ∼198.4 eV) and Ru-influenced Cl (ClRu 2p3/2 at ∼197.5 eV); Ru 3d3/2 binding energy shifts ∼0.3 eV due to Cl electronic modulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS analysis of the Cl 2p (Figure 1e) identifies two distinct Cl species: one corresponds to conventional Pt-Cl ligand (ClPt 2p3/2 at ∼198.4 eV), and another is influenced by Ru (ClRu 2p3/2 at ∼197.5 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Pt mass loading of 5.31 wt% in Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs and 4.76 wt% in Pt₁/Ru-NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry determines that the mass loading of Pt is ca. 5.31 wt% (Table S1) within Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Pt-Cl bending vibration at 185 cm⁻¹ for Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ, absent in Cl-free catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure 1c) shows an obvious vibration peak (Pt-Cl) at 185 cm⁻¹, assigned to Pt-Cl bending vibration.

nodes.characterization_summary: IR confirms Pt-Cl stretching vibration at 318 cm⁻¹ for Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Infrared spectroscopy (Figure 1d) confirms the existence of Pt-Cl stretching vibration peak at 318 cm⁻¹ for the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES shows white-line energy slightly lower than PtO₂ indicating Pt valence below +4; Ru K-edge shows negative shift indicating partial Ru reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray adsorption near-edge spectra (XANES, Figure 1f) indicate that the white-line energy feature at the Pt L₃-edge of the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ is slightly lower than that of PtO₂, demonstrating the Pt valence state below +4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge EXAFS FT shows dominant Pt-O peak at 1.67 Å (fitted 1.99 Å), no Pt-Pt; second-shell fitting reveals Pt-ClPt (R≈2.604 Å, N=0.9) and Pt-ClRu (R≈3.337 Å, N=1.6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through iterative refinements (Tables S4-S10) of second-shell EXAFS fitting, we ultimately achieved an appropriate fitting result (Figure 1h; Table S11), revealing two Pt-Cl coordination environments: Pt-ClPt (R≈2.604 Å, coordination number N = 0.9) and Pt-ClRu (R≈3.337 Å, N = 1.6).

Fourier transform of EXAFS data showing radial distribution

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Pt L₃-edge XANES shows Pt valence decreases from 2.5 to -0.3 over 2000 s HER at -0.05 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ normalized Pt L₃ edge XANES spectra (Figure 3a-c) reveal the valence states of Pt decrease from 2.5 to -0.3 over 2000 s HER at a constant potential of -0.05 V versus RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Pt L₃-edge EXAFS shows Pt-O diminishes, Pt-Ru emerges (CN from 2 to 5), Pt-Cl stabilizes at CN≈0.5 forming Pt-Cl-Pt structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From in situ EXAFS (Figure 3d), at open circuit potential (OCP), only Pt-O coordination is detected... the Pt-Cl signal appears with its CN stabilizing at approximately 0.5 upon the reduction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows Ru-O reduction and enhanced Pt-Cl bending vibration at 190 cm⁻¹ with Stark effect as potential decreases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman spectra (Figure 3f). As the potential decreases from 0.7 to 0 V, the Ru-O bond is gradually reduced, and the bending vibration peak of Pt-Cl near 190 cm⁻¹ becomes more pronounced.
